key_insight: SevenNet systematically underestimates vacancy formation energies in coronene, with larger deficits at increasingly under-coordinated edges, while closely matching mean Stone–Wales energies.
engineering_relevance: Universal MLIPs can accelerate graphene quantum-dot structure screening, but absolute vacancy energies and complex edge reconstructions still need DFT validation.
method: Benchmark SevenNet against spin-polarized PBE DFT for defects in coronene (C24H12).
Map site- and bond-resolved monovacancy, divacancy, and Stone–Wales energetics.
Compare 28 matched vacancy reconstructions using self-consistent chemical-potential reservoirs.
evidence_signal: SevenNet underestimates all 28 matched vacancy energies; mean deficits increase with broken edge C–H bonds from 0.30 to 0.74 eV for monovacancies and 0.65 to 1.11 eV for divacancies, versus a 0.013 eV difference in mean Stone–Wales energy.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to coronene; monitor symmetry-equivalent energy spreads for basin-sensitive relaxations and validate multi-basin edge configurations with DFT.
paper_title: Edge-scaling softening of a universal machine-learned potential: point-defect formation energies in a coronene graphene quantum dot
